You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-c4b91aa4: replicate a template across divider panels

Use when a grid is partitioned by complete straight divider lines (often color 6) into congruent rectangular panels, one panel contains a colored pattern, and the other panels are mostly a uniform blank/background (observed as 1). Copy the template panel's contents into each corresponding panel, preserving the divider lines.

## Validated behavior
- Demo: 5×9 input with a full vertical divider column of 3 at column 4. The 5×4 panel to the left was uniform 7 (blank), while the right 5×4 panel held a pattern. Output copied the right pattern into the left panel, preserving the divider. Pattern pixels were copied exactly, including its 7-valued cells; this is panel replication rather than recoloring.
- Fresh test: 11×13 input with full horizontal divider row 3 and full vertical divider column 6 (both color 6), forming four 3×6 panels with 3×6 content spans. The top-left panel contained a 3×6 template; remaining panels were blank 1s. Output tiled the exact 3×6 template into all four panels, preserving both divider lines. Accepted.

## Additional accepted fresh test
- A 17×11 grid had divider rows 5 and 11 and divider columns 3 and 7, all color 4, producing nine congruent 5×3 panels. The top-left panel contained a sparse pattern (7s and a 9) on background 1; the other eight panels were blank 1. The accepted output repeated the top-left panel's complete 5×3 contents into every panel, preserving all divider rows/columns. This confirms tiling across a 3×3 panel layout, not just a single split or a 2×2 layout.

## Procedure
1. Find complete divider rows/columns and treat them as immutable boundaries.
2. Identify congruent panel dimensions and locate the populated template panel.
3. Repeat the template panel's entire cell matrix into every other aligned panel, including template-colored/background cells; do not merely stamp non-background marks or recolor the blanks.
4. Preserve divider cells and validate dimensions and panel alignment before submitting.

Do not assume this rule for arbitrary grids without the full-divider/congruent-panel structure.
